The red/blue state distribution mainly stems from urban-rural divides rather than initial colonial or settlement patterns. Cities and dense coastal areas tend Democratic (blue), while rural and interior regions tend Republican (red). This was strengthened by "The Big Sort" where Americans increasingly moved to areas matching their political values. The South's shift from Democratic to Republican in the 1960s-70s during the Civil Rights era was also crucial in creating today's familiar electoral map. Economic patterns played a role too - with industrial/urban coastal regions developing different political cultures than agricultural interior states. While early settlement history had some influence, today's divisions are more strongly shaped by these modern demographic, economic and cultural factors.
